prompt: At a pizza shop, the number of toppings $X$ a customer orders has this distribution: $P(X = 1) = 0.2$, $P(X = 2) = 0.5$, $P(X = 3) = 0.3$. Find the mean $\mu_X$. Round to the nearest tenth.
hint: The mean of a discrete random variable is a weighted average: each value counts in proportion to its probability.

hints.text: The mean of a discrete random variable is a weighted average: each value counts in proportion to its probability.
Multiply each number of toppings by its probability and add the three products: $1(0.2) + 2(0.5) + 3(0.3)$.

explanation: The mean is $\mu_X = \sum x \cdot P(x)$, so multiply each value by its probability: $1(0.2) = 0.2$, $2(0.5) = 1.0$, $3(0.3) = 0.9$.
Adding the three weighted values gives $0.2 + 1.0 + 0.9 = 2.1$.
So $\mu_X = 2.1$ toppings. It need not be a whole number because it is a long-run average.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture 10 customers
steps: Among 10 typical customers, 2 order one topping, 5 order two, 3 order three.
